I'm thinking about how to map markers to their corresponding quadrants and their diagonally opposite positions. In demo1, the top-left and top-right markers were assigned to the same top quadrant, while demo2 had the top-right and bottom-right markers correspond to their respective quadrants. It seems like using the marker's location relative to the center will help in assigning them to their interior quadrants based on their row and column signs. I’ll also test markers in the bottom-left and bottom-right positions as well.

code='''def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if 5 in row]
    cols = [c for c in range(len(grid[0])) if any(grid[r][c] == 5 for r in range(len(grid)))]
    r0, r1 = min(rows), max(rows)
    c0, c1 = min(cols), max(cols)
    ri0, ri1 = r0 + 1, r1 - 1
    ci0, ci1 = c0 + 1, c1 - 1

    cm = (ci0 + ci1 + 1) // 2

        top = r < (r0 + r1) / 2
        left = c < (c0 + c1) / 2

                    ca, cb = (ci0, cm) if qc == 0 else (cm, ci1 + 1)
                    for rr in range(ra, rb):
                        for cc in range(ca, cb):
                            out[rr][cc] = color
    return out
'''

def transform(grid):
